independence_caveat: Same model family as the other reviewers; agreement is reading consistency, not independent validation.

findings.finding: KC1 states a conditional significance threshold but does not specify an executable raw-signal-to-observable chain: the raw velocity, photometry, and gas products; instrument calibration; reduction and deprojection; acceleration proxies; covariance; likelihood; and bias controls are not defined.
findings.source: snapshot.tex L192-L198 (KC1 wording, internal direction, and provenance gap)
findings.test: Pre-register the exact galaxy data release and raw products, velocity extraction and calibration, distance/inclination/beam or seeing corrections, baryonic mass model, nuisance priors, covariance, test statistic, and the fixed competing forward models before evaluating the >=5 sigma criterion.
findings.reasoning: The conditional logic is clear, but a significance threshold is downstream of a chosen data vector and reduction model. Without those choices, robust and bias-controlled are interpretive labels rather than an auditable measurement protocol; this limits testability without contradicting the conditional wording itself.

findings.finding: The reported >=5 sigma SPARC exclusion has no auditable signal-to-significance path: Delta-chi-squared and significance are null and the source is marked no new fit performed, so the underlying data, reductions, proxy construction, covariance, and alternative-model comparison cannot be checked.
findings.test: Retrieve the original fit or rerun it from the named data and code, including raw-data provenance, reduction choices, g_obs and g_bar construction, nuisance treatment, covariance, model degrees of freedom, and the pre-specified significance calculation; otherwise quarantine the sigma statement.
findings.reasoning: A null metadata field and no-new-fit status establish an evidential gap, not a null physical result. A sigma value is uninterpretable without the data release, likelihood, correlated errors, nuisance parameters, and the provenance of any fitted or fixed a0.

findings.finding: The SPARC/RAR proposal omits the raw-signal-to-proxy chain: line-of-sight HI or optical velocities and baryonic photometry/gas measurements must pass through instrument and reduction corrections to v(r), enclosed baryonic mass, g_obs = v^2/r, and g_bar, but none of those links or their error covariance is specified.
findings.source: snapshot.tex L214-L220 (proposed discriminator and SPARC/RAR preregistration conditions)
findings.test: Publish the complete forward and reduction pipeline from the fixed HI/optical and photometric/gas products to v(r), g_obs, and g_bar, with distance, inclination, beam/seeing, gas-conversion, stellar M/L, radial-binning, and covariance propagation, then evaluate the fixed model on a held-out sample.
findings.reasoning: The RAR is a relation between inferred accelerations, not a direct detector observable. Distance and inclination affect radii and velocities; photometry, gas calibration, and stellar M/L affect g_bar; shared inputs induce covariance. Without the chain, the test can select preprocessing assumptions rather than discriminate the EFC exponent.

findings.finding: a0 is a calibration scale entering the inferred acceleration relation, not a raw observable; the candidate set 1.2e-10, 6.5e-10, and a0_eff = C^2 a0 creates leakage risk unless its ancestry, calibration inputs, and freeze point are fixed before the fit.
findings.source: snapshot.tex L219-L220 (candidate a0 values, freeze condition, and required origin label)
findings.test: Label one a0 as MOND/SPARC input, EFC output, or nuisance calibration before viewing the holdout; freeze it, propagate distance/inclination/M/L/gas uncertainties, and report the result and sensitivity without re-estimating a0 on the test sample.
findings.reasoning: The manuscript correctly says the test is invalid until one value is frozen, but freezing a number does not make it independent. If a0 was selected or calibrated from the same RAR data or from the same baryonic assumptions, the apparent retrodiction is not a clean prediction. Its provenance must therefore be part of the measurement chain.

findings.finding: The mediator from the E-axis statement E proportional to sqrt(g) to a predicted RAR is not written: no field-to-acceleration solution, baryonic source model, boundary conditions, or likelihood mapping connects the exponent to g_obs and g_bar.
findings.source: snapshot.tex L166-L172 and L217-L220 (E-axis definition and claimed RAR discriminator)
findings.test: Derive and publish a dimensionally typed forward operator from the chosen EFC action and baryonic source to the predicted velocity field and RAR likelihood, including boundary conditions and nuisance parameters, then compare it against the fixed linear alternative on data not used to construct the operator.
findings.reasoning: An exponent choice is not by itself a velocity prediction. Different field equations, boundary conditions, source prescriptions, and nuisance treatments can produce different mu(g) mappings from the same exponent. Treating the RAR as a direct discriminator without this mediator hides theory dependence between model space and the measured proxies.

findings.finding: dL_GW/dL_EM is a model-derived proxy, not a raw observable: detector strain and electromagnetic photons or spectra become the two inferred distances through detector calibration, waveform and inclination inference, host/redshift association, cosmology or ladder assumptions, peculiar-velocity, lensing, and selection corrections, none of which is specified.
findings.source: snapshot.tex L214-L221 (siren proposal and distance-ratio expression)
findings.test: Pre-register the GW waveform and detector-calibration model, EM host/redshift and distance estimator, cosmology and ladder treatment, lensing and peculiar-velocity corrections, selection function, cross-covariance, and the posterior-level statistic for the distance ratio.
findings.reasoning: The displayed equation relates two inferred quantities and does not define the instrument-to-distance reductions. A distance mismatch can be generated by calibration, waveform, host, lensing, or cosmological systematics rather than propagation. The proposed test therefore needs a complete dual-channel measurement model before interpretation.

findings.finding: Freezing alpha, phi0, and phi(z) is necessary but not sufficient to make the siren ratio EFC-specific: the proposal still lacks a pre-data residual or likelihood, matched nuisance model, and alternative propagation hypotheses that could separate EFC coupling from GR systematics or other modified-gravity friction models.
findings.source: snapshot.tex L221 (explicit non-specificity and parameter-freeze condition)
findings.test: Freeze the field normalization and coupling trajectory before the sample is opened, then compare EFC, GR, and alternative propagation models with identical detector, waveform, host, cosmology, lensing, and selection nuisance parameters using a pre-specified posterior predictive or likelihood-ratio criterion.
findings.reasoning: The manuscript correctly retains the test as non-EFC-specific while the parameters are unfrozen. Measurement identifiability remains conditional even after freezing: the same inferred ratio can be explained by several propagation sectors or by channel-specific systematics unless the alternatives and nuisance treatment are fixed in advance.

findings.finding: The labels global screened limit and local low-acceleration (IR) response are not defined as pre-data measurable regimes by thresholds or observables for xi = |grad Phi|/a0, density, screening state, spatial scale, or averaging; they remain interpretive labels in the available text.
findings.source: snapshot.tex L89-L97 and L214-L234; C13 is only restated in the review-status region L281-L303, which is prior-review text and not used as independent evidence
findings.test: Before opening data, define xi, density and screening estimators from named raw measurements, set global/local thresholds and spatial averaging rules, specify the instrument and reduction pipeline, and blind-apply the regime classifier to held-out observations with a declared observable likelihood.
findings.reasoning: A regime statement becomes empirical only when state variables and decision boundaries are fixed before data. xi depends on an inferred potential and a0; density and screening can be model-dependent; global versus local requires a scale and boundary convention. Without those definitions, MOND-like and LCDM-like can be assigned after seeing the pattern.

findings.finding: No target observable or equal-footing comparison is specified that would distinguish a global screened limit from a local low-acceleration response on the same raw data; the two candidate regimes could therefore be relabelings of shared inferred proxies.
findings.source: snapshot.tex L214-L234 and L281-L303 (the latter is review-status text only and is not treated as evidence)
findings.test: Specify a regime-discriminating observable, common raw data and instrument reductions, matched nuisance and covariance models, and a blind holdout criterion comparing the global and local forward predictions against each other and against GR/MOND baselines.
findings.reasoning: The manuscript declares no executed selection or independent validation and supplies no regime-specific likelihood in the test sections. A resemblance to LCDM or MOND is not a measurement result unless the forward predictions differ on a declared observable and the comparison uses the same data and nuisance treatment.
